conventions: The וְהָיָה כִּי protasis opened at DEU.6.10 runs through DEU.6.11 and finds its apodosis at DEU.6.12, which the ASV opens with *then*. No conjunction morpheme stands in DEU.6.12 — the clause begins with the imperative הִשָּׁמֶר — and rule 10 keeps the הָיָה of DEU.6.10 inside its own verse, so that *then* is its own `added` unit under rule 14. Do not restore it to the הָיָה frame of DEU.6.10, which holds only *it shall be* because the ASV writes no *that* (rule 45), and do not fold it into the imperative or into the לְ of לְךָ: the only morpheme that could have licensed it stands in another verse.

Supplied English prepositions in this chapter are placed by what licenses them, not by position. One written before a nominal whose own case-function licenses it joins that nominal under rule 33 — אֶרֶץ → *in a land* (6.3), מָחָר → *in time to come* (6.20), יוֹם → *at ... day* (6.24, the כְּ beside it already holding its own *as*). The *of* of מְלֵאִים כָּל־טוּב → *houses full of all good things* instead joins מָלֵא, on rule 44's reasoning that a preposition the ASV writes to reach a governing word's complement belongs to that word's unit: מְלֵאִים is absolute (Aampa), so no construct relation stands for rule 19 to place the *of* on, and English *full* selects the word rather than the nominal stating what it contributes. The competing reading, giving the *of* to כֹּל as rule 33's opening word of the phrase, is recorded in that verse's note.

כָּל־הַיָּמִים → *always* is aligned as a two-morpheme fusion of כֹּל and יָמִים, headed on יָמִים, with the separately segmented article its own `unrepresented` unit because the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase. That follows rule 30's explicit ruling on דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים → *chronicles*, which keeps a separately segmented article out of such a fusion. Corpus precedent for the same Hebrew phrase rendered *for ever* runs the other way, reading all three morphemes as one `noncompositional` unit headed on *ever* in seven units including DEU.4.40 and 1KI.11.39. The binding rule was followed over the precedent here; anyone revisiting this should change the rule and the corpus together rather than one chapter at a time.
report: Checked all 41 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket traces to an ASV difference the source licenses: לְ before an infinitive takes the word actually written (to at 6.1/6.2/6.3/6.10/6.19/6.23-25, that where the ASV recasts finitely at 6.1/6.24, unrepresented at 6.20 for לֵאמֹר, rule 52); a dative לְ+suffix is unrepresented only where the ASV writes a bare indirect object (6.10, 6.23, 6.24) and takes unto where it writes one (6.25, rule 40); הַ is unrepresented only where another morpheme holds the phrase's one written determiner (6.6, 6.24, 6.25) or where a coordinated article repeats one already rendered (6.18), per rules 41 and 47.

Positive cross-verse checks that passed: יִיטַב לְךָ is divided identically at 6.3 and 6.18 (it may be well headed on well by rule 44, with on the לְ); לְמַעַן is counted the same way at 6.2 (two particles, two written that's), 6.18 (one particle whose that the ASV rewrites over the coordinated clause, rule 55) and 6.23; the construct-plus-article count is uniform at 6.12, 6.14, 6.15 and 6.17 (a present article takes the the standing before its own word, the construct takes a supplied one, rule 29); כַּאֲשֶׁר is fused to as and headed on כְּ in all four occurrences; the object marker is unrepresented in all eleven, its suffix carrying the pronoun wherever one is written.

The added sweep, which the lemma table cannot see: them (6.1), it (6.3) and him (6.16) are supplied object pronouns with no object morpheme in their clauses (rule 44); then (6.12) is a supplied apodosis connective in a clause opening with a bare imperative; mean (6.20) is a supplied lexical verb in a verbless clause whose only morpheme, מָה, is already fully rendered What (rule 20). Read end to end, no verse folds a comparable supplied word into a neighbouring morpheme, so no split hides behind the clean table.

The one place supplied prepositions are treated two ways is licensed by the source, not a split: 6.3, 6.20 and 6.24 put in a land, in time to come and at this day on the nominal whose own case-function licenses them (rule 33), while 6.11 puts the of of full of all good things on מָלֵא, whose English rendering selects it, מְלֵאִים being absolute (Aampa) so that rule 19 has no construct relation to place it on. Both readings are named in 6.11's note; the line the chapter drew is now in the conventions log rather than left to be rediscovered.

BSB: none of the 22 disagreements is an error. The paragogic nun (rule 32, 6.2/6.3/6.14/6.17), the eleven unrendered articles (rules 41, 47), the five unrepresented לְ (rules 27, 40, 52), the object marker at 6.23 (rule 16) and the reflexive suffix of הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ at 6.12, for which the ASV writes no pronoun at all, are all documented convention differences. No accepted edge was moved.

Flagged and left alone: 6.24 aligns כָּל־הַיָּמִים as a two-morpheme fusion with the separately segmented article unrepresented, following rule 30's explicit chronicles ruling, whereas corpus precedent for the same phrase as for ever keeps the article inside a three-morpheme noncompositional unit headed on ever (7 units, including DEU.4.40). The binding rule was followed over the precedent; the tension is recorded so a later pass changes both together.

No promotions. The 6.11 of would need rule 44's supplied-preposition clause widened from a verb to a governing predicate adjective, and this chapter has one occurrence and the packet no מָלֵא precedent — too thin to bind every later chapter, so the contract is left as it stands.
